subject: Prefix-cache assumptions + budget check — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finmetrics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: prefix-cache assumptions + budget check

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the specific asks we said we would follow up on so you can share with Aaron/procurement: 

1) Customer inputs we captured on the call
- Expected monthly query volume: ~28M requests (you mentioned ~500k DAU with avg 56 requests/user/month).
- Average prompt length: ~80 tokens; average completion length: ~150 tokens (ballpark).
- Top 10 intents account for ~42% of calls (good candidate for prefix caching).

2) Budget & target unit economics
- You said target effective unit-cost: approximately $40–$60 per 1M effective tokens served to users (post-cache).
- Confirming procurement prefers a 3-scenario view (conservative / expected / optimistic) for effective $/1M given different cache hit rates.

3) Our high-level caching assumptions (what we’ll model next)
- Prefix cache strategy: canonicalize and cache the first N tokens of prompt + intent key. Initial pilot N = 64 tokens for intent-heavy flows.
- Hit-rate sensitivity: we'll model 20%, 35%, 55% hit-rate buckets (cold/warm/optimized).
- Effective cost formula we'll use: effective_cost_per_1M = list_model_cost_per_1M * (1 - hit_rate) + amortized_cache_storage_and_infra_per_1M

4) Next steps (what we’ll deliver ~48 hours)
- Jordan: share an initial 3-scenario cost table (attached spreadsheet) and a short one-pager on prefix selection tradeoffs (attached PDF).
- Marissa: confirm engineering feasibility for our proposed prefix key and estimate expected hit-rate range from pilot data patterns.
- Rachel: produce a quote/term sheet for the 3 scenarios and note any volume commit discounts that change effective $/1M.

Attachments: finmetrics_token_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet with the numbers I entered live), redwood_prefix_cache_plan.pdf (short note on prefix selection and storage assumptions).

A couple specific clarifying questions for you / Aaron to confirm:
- Is the 500k DAU estimate the steady-state assumption for pricing, or an ARR ramp milestone?
- Any regulatory constraints on caching returned completions or must we only cache prompts/prefixes?

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min follow to walk through the three-scenario numbers once you’ve had a look.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0191

--Attachment: redwood_prefix_cache_plan.pdf (PDF, 62KB)

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finmetrics.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: prefix-cache assumptions + budget check

Thanks Jordan — useful recap and the attachments look good at a glance. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 500k DAU is our steady-state target for FY27 (we'll likely ramp across Q4/1). For initial pilots in Q3 we expect ~120k DAU. Please show both pilot and steady-state rows in the spreadsheet.
- We can cache prompts/prefixes and intent keys; we cannot cache full completion text longer than 1 minute retention unless it is anonymized (legal constraint). So model caching primarily on prefix/pattern matches.
- Procurement (Aaron) asked for a simple three-line table showing effective $/1M at hit-rates 20%, 40%, 60% and a compute/storage split.

Can you please provide those three scenarios with the assumptions visible inline? Aaron — looping you in for budget/PO expectations.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Director of AI Products | FinMetrics
samantha.ortiz@finmetrics.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finmetrics.com>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@finmetrics.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap: prefix-cache assumptions + budget check — three-scenario costing (draft)

Marissa / Rachel — forwarding Sam/Aaron with the ask. Draft numbers below (internal assumptions noted). Please sanity-check & convert to a customer-facing table.

Quick assumptions used (internal):
- List model cost (hosted list price for candidate model): $18.00 per 1M tokens (this is the list model unit).
- Amortized cache infra & storage per 1M effective tokens (estimated): $0.80 per 1M (includes S3/redis + bandwidth + maintenance amortized over volume).
- Effective cost formula: effective = list_price * (1 - hit_rate) + cache_amortized_per_1M

Scenario calculations (example rows to send to customer):
- Conservative (hit_rate = 20%): effective = 18.00 * (1 - 0.20) + 0.80 = 18.00 * 0.80 + 0.80 = 14.40 + 0.80 = $15.20 per 1M tokens
- Expected (hit_rate = 40%): effective = 18.00 * 0.60 + 0.80 = 10.80 + 0.80 = $11.60 per 1M tokens
- Optimistic (hit_rate = 60%): effective = 18.00 * 0.40 + 0.80 = 7.20 + 0.80 = $8.00 per 1M tokens

Compute vs storage split (approx):
- Conservative (20%): compute portion = $14.40, cache infra = $0.80
- Expected (40%): compute portion = $10.80, cache infra = $0.80
- Optimistic (60%): compute portion = $7.20, cache infra = $0.80

Notes / engineering caveats for Marissa:
- The cache amortized figure assumes warm cache on 70% of traffic after 90 days of training + TTLs tuned to 24–72 hours for high-frequency intents. If TTLs are shorter (e.g., <1h), expected hit-rate over time drops ~5–12 percentage points depending on traffic shape.
- Prefix length: at 64 tokens we expect higher collision resistance but larger storage per cache key; at 32 tokens we reduce storage but may reduce hit rate by ~6–10% on our initial dataset. We should include both 32/64 token rows in the final note.
- Cold-start impact: first 2–3 days pilot will have significantly lower hit rates — include a conservative ramp in the spreadsheet.

Sam / Aaron — does the above mapping (list price $18 + $0.80 cache amortization) look reasonable directionally? We'll update the customer-facing table based on Marissa/Rachel feedback and send a cleaned PDF/quote by EOD.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
